fixes_applied.description: Original recoloring `td.df.loc[pair[0],'label'] = td.df.loc[pair[0]]['label'].apply(...)` misaligns on the concat MultiIndex under modern pandas (2.x) and silently sets the ENTIRE label column to NaN. That both destroys the 4-color mapping (all points one color) AND makes kaleido crash with 'Transform failed 525: Cannot read property length of null' on the all-null color array. Replaced with a positional numpy remap: _m0 = index.get_level_values(0)==pair[0]; label = where(_m0, where(lab==1,BLUE,RED), where(lab==1,YELLOW,PURPLE)). Verified 4 distinct color values, 0 NaN.

- td.df.loc[pair[1],'label'] = td.df.loc[pair[1]]['label'].apply(lambda x: YELLOW if x==1 else PURPLE)
+ _lab=td.df['label'].values; _m0=td.df.index.get_level_values(0)==pair[0]
+ td.df['label']=np.where(_m0, np.where(_lab==1,BLUE,RED), np.where(_lab==1,YELLOW,PURPLE))

step_outcomes.notes: Reproduces the paper's central generalization result (Fig 5). 13B heatmap signatures match the paper: train larger_than alone -> 1% on smaller_than (LR) / 7% (MM) [spurious single-polarity direction]; train larger_than+smaller_than -> 100% both. Train cities alone -> 28% on neg_cities (no negation handling); cities+neg_cities -> 99-100% on neg_cities, sp_en_trans, etc. Cross-domain transfer strong: 13B LR(cities+neg_cities)->sp_en_trans = 99.7%. Scale trend clear: every OOD average is higher at 13B than 7B (e.g. cities+neg_cities 0.68->0.83). Split seed fixed at 42 for reproducibility (a setup value; the notebook uses a random seed each run, so exact per-cell values will vary by a few tenths of a percent with the split).

fixes_applied.description: few_shot.py uses the pre-0.2 nnsight runner API: `with model.forward(output_hidden_states=True, remote=..., remote_include_output=...) as runner: with runner.invoke(prompt): pass`, `runner.output['past_key_values']`, and passing past_key_values back into model.forward. nnsight 0.2.21 has no such runner wrapper -- model.forward proxies to LlamaForCausalLM.forward and rejects `remote` (TypeError). Reimplemented with the working nnsight 0.2.21 trace API used elsewhere in the repo: for each held-out query, trace `prompt + statement`, save model.lm_head.output[:, -1, :], and compute diff = P(' TRUE') - P(' FALSE'); gamma = median(diffs); predict diff > gamma. Dropped only the KV-cache reuse optimization (recompute the 5-shot prefix per batch), which produces identical logits. Output JSON schema unchanged.
fixes_applied.original_error: TypeError: LlamaForCausalLM.forward() got an unexpected keyword argument 'remote'
fixes_applied.diff_snippet:
- with model.forward(...remote...) as runner:
-     with runner.invoke(batch...): logits = model.lm_head.output; ...
+ with model.trace([prompt+s for s in batch], scan=False, validate=False):
+     last = model.lm_head.output[:, -1, :].save()
+ diff = last.value.softmax(-1)[:,true_idx] - [:,false_idx]

step_outcomes.notes: Reproduces the paper's few-shot baseline pattern: strong on affirmative datasets (cities 0.99, sp_en_trans 1.00 on 13B) but FAILS on negated/opposite datasets -- neg_cities 0.31 (below chance), smaller_than 0.48. This is exactly the paper's contrast: trained probes generalize across negation (Step 4) while calibrated few-shot does not. 7B uniformly worse than 13B (neg_cities 0.21, smaller_than 0.50) -> same scale trend. Shot sampling seed fixed at 42 (setup value; original uses df.sample with no seed, so exact accuracies depend on which 5 shots are drawn). n_query counts are (dataset rows - 5 shots). counterfact evaluated at full 31959 queries.

fixes_applied.description: Wrote an orchestrator to load 13B once instead of the CLI's ~48 reloads (~2.5h saved). First run OOMed on the A40: probe training needs autograd, but leaving grad enabled made the intervention forward passes build a full autograd graph over the 13B model (26GB model -> 44GB, OOM). Fixed by t.set_grad_enabled(False) globally and wrapping only the probe-training call in `with t.enable_grad()`; direction cast to cuda:0/bf16 for in-place add.

step_outcomes.notes: Reproduces the paper's central causal result (Table 2 / Section 4): the mass-mean (MM) truth direction is strongly causal -- adding it to false sp_en_trans statements flips P(TRUE)-P(FALSE) most of the way to the true baseline (NIE f->t 0.72-0.88; t->f 0.52-0.98). LR directions are weaker/more variable (0.03-0.31), CCS moderate -- consistent with the paper's finding that MM directions are more causally faithful than LR. The 'none' baselines are identical across cells (PD-=-0.914, PD+=0.793) as expected (intervention adds 0). 70B rows of Table 2 not attempted (no local weights). Exact NIE magnitudes depend on the probe-direction scaling; qualitative MM>LR causal ordering matches the paper.

step_outcomes.notes: Reproduces the paper's activation-patching localization (Fig 6/7, C6+C7). 13B cities heatmap shows: strong TRUE-FALSE signal at the SUBJECT token ('Chicago') in early layers (0-7), moving to the OBJECT/period tokens ('Canada','.') in middle layers (7-17), then a strong dark column at the FINAL token (':' of 'This statement is:') in late layers (14-39) -- i.e. statement-level truth info is summarized over the end-of-sentence/final token in later layers (C7). Same qualitative structure in sp_en_trans and in 7B, but 7B effects are much weaker (max logit diff 1.25 vs 13B 4.12) -> scale trend. 70B not attempted (no local weights).
